title: A router beside a production model
subtitle: Serving two thousand concurrent agents from a 0.6B model in the memory left over on a shared GPU, and reporting the target I missed

stats.label: the engine's whole footprint beside a 30B model
requests served during the largest burst
answers failed, rejected or contaminated in that burst

lede: The tool-discovery model had to live on a GPU whose memory belonged to a 30-billion-parameter serving model. I set two thousand concurrent clients as an acceptance requirement, and built an engine that admits work against measured memory and refuses with a number when it cannot. The sustained throughput target I had pre-registered for mixed traffic was missed by a wide margin, for a reason I can name, and that miss is on this page. A discovery model that agents call before most actions will be called by many agents at once. If it falls over under load, every agent stalls at the same moment.
quote: The miss is structural, and saying so is more useful to the next design than a better-looking number.
evidence: Inference serving architecture: a batched continuous-decode engine with paged key-value memory, 2.7 GiB in total beside a 30B model on one shared GPU.
Admission control under memory pressure: requests admitted against measured free memory and refused as a typed busy response with a number when they do not fit.
Load testing methodology: a ladder from one to 2,048 clients with abort conditions, 85.9 requests a second in the largest burst and 0 answers failed, rejected or contaminated.
Capacity reporting: a pre-registered sustained throughput target for mixed traffic reported as missed, with its cause, instead of a friendlier accounting of about 14 requests a second.
author: Corey James
